thread.title: Dow Jones Lags; Will This Tech Beat Apple? | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones Lags; Will This Tech Beat Apple? | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average erased moderate losses and rose bullishly to session highs as technology firms — including Apple, Microsoft and Intel — rallied to offset a broad decline in the retail sector. Consumer-spending-focused names also dominated the downside in stocks today .
X Stocks immediately swung higher on a report that the head of the Atlanta Federal Reserve cautioned against an overly aggressive policy toward raising interest rates. Wire services, meanwhile, are reporting the possibility of progress on trade talks between the U.S. and other key economic partners ahead of a G20 meeting set for Nov. 30 in Buenos Aires.
Meanwhile, data networking equipment titan Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) jumped more than 4% and briefly moved back above the 50-day moving average.
Internet gear makers were not the only techs to rally sharply. Among IBD's 197 industry groups , top performers included semiconductor equipment, fabless chips, database software, gaming software and enterprise software. All of these groups rose 2% or more.
In Leaderboard, new member Twilio ( TWLO ) retook its recent buy point of 88.98 in a cup base. Shares jumped more than 8% to 90.81 in heavy volume.
Notice on a daily chart how the expert in desktop and mobile notification technology has held above its 50-day moving average throughout the recent sharp pullback. That's bullish.
Cisco Vs. Apple While a strong move past the 50-day line would add a more bullish tone to Cisco's chart, the internet and telecom gear giant's action since the start of October has certainly been far better than Apple ( AAPL ) so far in Q4.
One reason: Cisco has treated its longer-term 200-day moving average as a floor of institutional buying support. That's bullish. Apple, however, has pierced through its 200-day line for the first time in more than six months. The megacap tech is now clearly working on a new base .
Other Key Stock Indexes Beat The Dow At around 2 p.m. ET, the Nasdaq composite stormed more than 1.5% higher after falling 0.9% in a volatile, seesawing session Wednesday. As IBD's The Big Picture column noted, the weakness in most FANG stocks has contributed to the disappointing action by the Nasdaq since it went into a full-blown correction in early October. But Thursday's action points to a positive reversal.
The Nasdaq 100 rallied more than 1.4%, while the S&P 500 jumped nearly 0.8%. Volume is running mildly lower vs. the same time on Wednesday on both main exchanges, but appears to be accelerating with less than two hours left in the session.
The small-cap S&P 600 is trying to halt a five-day slide, rising 1%. At 956, the 600 is up 2% since Jan. 1. The index initially lost nearly 0.8% before rebounding.
Will Cisco Beat Apple In The Next 12 Months? Cisco also shows a stronger Relative Price Strength Rating of 85 on a scale of 1 (awful) to 99 (awesome) over the past 12 months. Apple's RS Rating, as seen in IBD Stock Checkup , has slipped to a 72 from as high as 94 over the past eight weeks.
Late Wednesday, Cisco posted a 23% jump in fiscal first-quarter earnings to 75 cents a share. That marked the biggest year-over-year gain in at least 20 quarters. Revenue rose 8% and marked a fourth quarter in a row of top-line growth acceleration.
The Risk With Apple Fundamentals Apple, meanwhile, shows signs that its earnings increases will slow in the next two fiscal years ending in September. (Read more details in this Stock Market Today column .)
Both Cisco and Apple hold a slot within the Dow Jones industrial average, which fell less than 0.5% in midafternoon trading. Consumer and retail components within the 30-stock Dow were among the day's worst performers, including Home Depot ( HD ), Nike ( NKE ) and Walmart ( WMT ).
All three declined 1 point or more. Walmart reported a 1% increase in sales for the October-ended fiscal third quarter and an 8% pickup in earnings to $1.08 a share. Walmart fell 2% to 99.39 to slip mildly below a 100.31 entry point in a long saucer with handle base.
Earlier in the day, stocks looked set for a sluggish open following news that U.S. retail sales jumped 0.8% in October vs. the prior month, beating the Econoday estimate of up 0.5%. But core sales excluding autos and gas rose 0.3% and missed the Wall Street view of a 0.4% increase.
Retail, Consumer Stock Leaders Backtrack In IBD Leaderboard , some consumer-spending-oriented stocks remain in basing mode.
Lululemon ( LULU ), the innovator of high-priced yogawear, dropped more than 2%, but volume is running below normal levels. The market leader, which joined IBD's Leaderboard in March during a pullback to the 10-week moving average near 78, has been fashioning a potential new base since peaking at 164.79 on Oct. 1.
The drop from that high has been limited to just 19%. The large-cap stock, with a market value approaching $17 billion, is spending its sixth week below the 10-week line. A prolonged period below the 10-week moving average, such as more than eight or nine weeks, would indicate a deeper and longer correction is likely.
Five Below ( FIVE ), which ranks No. 2 in the IBD 50, sank more than 3% to 118.99. The variety retail chain has bobbed above and below its 50-day moving average in recent weeks. Ollie's Bargain Outlet ( OLLI ) dropped nearly 4%. But it's held up better than most key equity indexes. At 87.56, the deep-discount chain trades just 10% beneath its all-time high of 97.61.
In Other Financial Markets Elsewhere, crude oil futures rebounded 0.6% to $56.62 a barrel but remain more than 25% below a year-to-date peak of $76.
Long-dated U.S. government bonds rallied, sending the yield on the benchmark Treasury 10-year note down 3 basis points to 3.09%.
